comparison: Perfect agreement. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support the observational claims about heterogeneity in worm behavior (C1, C2, C20-C22, C29). Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge this as a 'key observation' and 'prominent feature of the empirical data.'

Strong agreement on core modeling results (C3-C5, C18, C38-C41, C47-C50). Both find the model well-supported and convincing. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative fit to data; peer reviewers confirm the model 'performs well' and 'matches the data,' though Reviewer 2 raises a philosophical concern about potential circularity in fitting.

Both address the key mechanistic insight about stochastic sampling producing apparent transitions (C51-C54). OpenEval finds this well-supported by Figure 2f; peer reviewers accept this as 'a strong argument that apparent state changes can arise as an epiphenomenon of stochastic processes.'

Strong agreement on model comparison results (C56-C66). Both support the conclusion that non-binary models outperform binary models. OpenEval cites quantitative evidence (JSD values, p<0.001); peer reviewers implicitly accept this by endorsing the single-state model over two-state alternatives.

Perfect agreement. Both rate claims about pheromone effects (C42-C46) as uncertain/speculative. OpenEval notes the explanation is 'reasonable but unvalidated'; peer reviewers treat this as a methodological consideration without challenging it.

Perfect agreement. Both support the conceptual implications (C67-C72) about simplification and mechanistic parsimony. OpenEval finds these logically follow from model success; peer reviewers explicitly endorse that 'simple neuronal mechanisms can drive behavioral sequences that appear more complex.'

Significant disagreement. OpenEval supports the biological interpretation of M (C73-C77) as reasonable and mathematically correct. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, stating 'there is no obvious candidate for the neuronal basis of the decaying factor M' and that this 'weakens the case for the model.'

Disagreement on neural mechanism claims (C78-C91). OpenEval finds the connection to neural circuits from López-Cruz et al. well-supported and reasonable. Peer reviewers find this uncertain, noting 'contradictory evidence' that undermines the hypothesis linking M to sensory neuron activity.

Disagreement on complexity of neural mechanisms (C92-C98). OpenEval supports these as providing important context about multi-level decay. Peer reviewers specifically critique this discussion, finding the evidence about glutamatergic signaling and sensory neuron depolarization 'contradictory' and problematic.

Partial overlap on limitations and future directions (C99-C102, with C101 shared). OpenEval supports these as appropriately identifying limitations. Peer reviewers express stronger concern, questioning 'what insight the model provides' absent an underlying mechanism.

Agreement on conceptual framework (C6, C16-C17). OpenEval finds the hypothesis well-supported by modeling results. Peer reviewers affirm this, with the editor stating authors 'provide convincing evidence' for the single-state interpretation.

OpenEval supports background and context claims (C7-C15) about biological context and stochastic reorientations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically address these background claims.

OpenEval supports methodological description and critique (C19, C23-C28) of López-Cruz et al. classification approach. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically address these methodological critiques.

Partial overlap on methodological justification (C33, C36). OpenEval supports these as providing important context for the Gillespie algorithm approach. Peer reviewers find the methodology 'well described' but raise conceptual concerns about circularity in the fitting process.

Peer reviewers evaluate methodological claims (C30-C32, C34-C35, C37) about the Gillespie algorithm implementation. While OpenEval R2 includes these claims, peer R8 specifically focuses on methodology description, finding it well-described but questioning potential circularity.
